Title: Dr Yasmin Amarsi honoured by McMaster University
NewsSummary: Dr Yasmin Amarsi, Founding Dean, Aga Khan University School of Nursing and Midwifery, East Africa, has been awarded an honorary Doctor of Science degree by McMaster University, Canada.
NewsContent:
Dr Yasmin Amarsi, Founding Dean, Aga Khan University School of Nursing and Midwifery, East Africa, has been awarded an honorary Doctor of Science degree by McMaster University, Canada. This prestigious award is bestowed on individuals who have made noteworthy impact in public service or other areas at national or international levels.

Dr Amarsi completed her General Nursing and Midwifery Diplomas from the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre, Karachi, Pakistan in 1972 and 1975 respectively. She then went on to complete her BScN degree from McMaster University in 1985 as part of a partnership between AKU and McMaster. She was the first AKU instructor to graduate from McMaster through this partnership.  Dr Amarsi completed her Master of Science degree in Education and Administration from University of Arizona in 1983, and her PhD in Health Human Resource Development and Programme Evaluation from McMaster University in 1998.

Since 1980, Dr Amarsi has served Aga Khan University School of Nursing in various capacities. She grew from a faculty member in the nursing diploma and Bachelor of Science programme to join the University's leadership team. From 1998 to 2008, she was the top executive at the School of Nursing, first as Director, then Associate Dean, and then finally as Dean. During her time with AKU-SON, Dr Amarsi responded on behalf of AKU to the demand from various countries, where the Aga Khan Development Network is active, to support new and growing nursing initiatives. She played a direct role in influencing governments in nursing education and service policy, and also contributed her expertise in other areas that have led to the development and improved status of the nursing profession. This year, she has been appointed to lead the development of a new Aga Khan University School of Nursing and Midwifery in Nairobi.
